summary: Olen keeps the Holy Breeze on its cliffs: shrines and cisterns, the old quiet with Nafeher, the wardens of Mirolon or a wall behind the cliffs, the Breeze healers, and shrines that shelter the refugees of the march.

breeze_keepers.name: The Breeze-Keepers
breeze_keepers.desc: The keepers of the cliff shrines tend the evening wind with song and lamp, and teach the pilgrims how to feel it on their faces. A land that prays in one voice is slow to quarrel.

breeze_and_lamp.name: The Breeze and the Lamp
breeze_and_lamp.desc: Healers of the Houses of the First Light work beside the shrines, with their lamps, their herbs and their patient hands. Fewer children die in Olen than in any land for a hundred leagues.

breeze_alone.name: The Breeze Alone
breeze_alone.desc: Olen keeps its own shrines and its own healers, and welcomes nobody else's. The Holy Breeze is enough, say the keepers, and the pilgrims go home.

cliff_terraces_spirit.name: Cliff Terraces
cliff_terraces_spirit.desc: Terrace upon terrace of barley and beans climbs the cliffs, held by walls of dry stone and watered from the cisterns. Olen eats well in a land where almost no one else does.

breeze_markets_spirit.name: Breeze Markets
breeze_markets_spirit.desc: A market is held every evening when the cool wind rises, under awnings of sail-cloth. Traders come from the Dominion and from Mirolon, and nobody asks where the others are from.

cliffs_hold.name: The Cliffs Hold
cliffs_hold.desc: The cliffs are walled at every landing and fortified at every pass. Whatever comes from the sea will find the cliffs a good deal taller than expected.

breeze_healers_spirit.name: The Breeze Healers
breeze_healers_spirit.desc: Healers walk the cliff roads with lamps and herb-bags, tending the sick of every folk and every land. The hurt of Olen are cared for, and so are the hurt of its neighbours.

sea_watch_spirit.name: The Sea Watch
sea_watch_spirit.desc: Lamps burn on the cliff-tops through the night, and watchers sit beside each. A hull on the horizon is seen long before it can be named.

guard_of_the_breeze_spirit.name: Guard of the Breeze
guard_of_the_breeze_spirit.desc: The guard of the cliff shrines wear white and carry long spears. They are few, but they are devoted, and they stand where they are told to stand.

hold_the_cliffs_spirit.name: Hold the Cliffs
hold_the_cliffs_spirit.desc: Every landing is manned, every path watched and every shrine garrisoned. The Breeze blows on, and Olen holds the cliffs it blows over.

breeze_rises.title: The Evening Breeze
breeze_rises.desc: The cool wind rises off the sea, as it does every evening, and the people of the cliff-towns come out of their houses to feel it. Olena asks the keepers what the Breeze would have the shrines do.

rumours_from_nafeher.title: Rumours from Nafeher
rumours_from_nafeher.desc: Traders bring word that the galleys of Dolon are buying more salt than a peaceful land eats, and that the storms over Nafeher have not lifted in a year. The keepers do not say what they think.

olen_offers_tribute.title: Tribute from Olen
olen_offers_tribute.desc: A string of mules from Olen arrives at the border of the Dominion, loaded with salt, dried fish and a small chest of silver. The keepers ask for nothing but the old quiet.

options.name: Nafeher takes no gifts from the north.

olen_offers_friendship.title: Friendship from Olen
olen_offers_friendship.desc: Envoys of Olen stand in the lake-hall of Mirolon, in white cloaks and with a lamp between them. They offer the wardens a friendship as constant as the evening wind.

an_answer_on_the_wind.title: An Answer on the Wind
an_answer_on_the_wind.desc: The answer has come back on the evening wind, and it is yes. The keepers read it in the faces of the envoys before a word is spoken.

the_wind_falls_still.title: The Wind Falls Still
the_wind_falls_still.desc: The envoys come back with nothing. The wind falls still over the cliffs, and the keepers go quietly to their shrines.

focuses.name: The Holy Breeze
focuses.desc: Each evening a cool wind rises off the sea, the only cool air for a hundred leagues, and Olena of the Holy Breeze goes to the cliff-top shrine to meet it. The people say that the wind is a gift, and the freeholders of Olen believe them.

focuses.name: Olena's Counsel
focuses.desc: Olena has kept the chief shrine since she was a girl and knows every verse of the Breeze's songs. Her counsel is gentle, brief and almost always followed.

focuses.name: The Breeze Shrines
focuses.desc: Small shrines are built on every cliff-top, each with a cup for the wind and a lamp for the night. The keepers tend them, and the pilgrims leave gifts.

focuses.name: The Breeze-Keepers
focuses.desc: The keepers of the shrines form a body with its own rule and its own hymns. They are the heart of Olen's quiet, and the quiet is the heart of Olen.

focuses.name: The Breeze and the Lamp
focuses.desc: Healers of the Houses of the First Light are welcomed beside the shrines, with their lamps, their herbs and their grain-stores. The keepers are divided about them, but the sick are glad.

focuses.name: The Breeze Alone
focuses.desc: Olen keeps its own shrines and its own healers. The keepers say that the Breeze needs no lamps but its own, and the visitors are courteously escorted home.

focuses.name: Olen at Peace
focuses.desc: The shrines are tended, the terraces are green and the evening wind comes on time. Olen is at peace, and it knows what that is worth.

focuses.name: Cliff Terraces
focuses.desc: The cliffs of Olen are cut into terraces and held by walls of dry stone. Cistern-water runs down them in channels, and barley grows where no barley should.

focuses.name: Windmills of the Cliffs
focuses.desc: Windmills crown the cliff-tops, turning in the sea breeze and grinding grain, pumping water and driving a hundred small machines. The mills of Olen are slow, steady and always turning.

focuses.name: Cistern Roads
focuses.desc: Roads are cut beside the cistern channels, so that water and wagons share the same level path. Marra Cisternwright walks them every spring and mends what the rains have broken.

focuses.name: The Cool Harbour
focuses.desc: A harbour is cut into the foot of the cliffs, where the cool wind blows into the water and keeps the heat at bay. The galleys of the Dominion buy salt there and ask nothing.

focuses.name: Breeze Markets
focuses.desc: A market is held every evening when the cool wind rises, under awnings of sail-cloth. Traders from Mirolon and the south sell side by side and compare their prices.

focuses.name: Olen Prospers
focuses.desc: Terraces, mills and markets bring coin to Olen, and the keepers of the shrines remember to give some of it back to the Breeze. The cisterns are enlarged and the lamps are lit.

focuses.name: The Southern Storm
focuses.desc: The storms over Nafeher have not lifted in a year, and the galleys of Dolon are buying more salt than a peaceful land eats. The keepers of the shrines watch the southern sky and say little.

focuses.name: Keep the Old Quiet
focuses.desc: Olen has kept the old quiet with Nafeher for generations: a tribute of salt and dried fish, and in return no questions. The keepers agree to send it again.

focuses.name: Stand with the Wardens
focuses.desc: Mirolon's wardens hold the lake towns against the storm, and Olen is asked to stand beside them. The keepers vote to send an answer on the evening wind.

focuses.name: Behind Our Cliffs
focuses.desc: Olen decides to trust nobody and wall itself behind the cliffs. Every landing is fortified, every path is watched and the shrines keep their lamps lit through the night.

focuses.name: The Quiet Kept
focuses.desc: Nafeher has accepted Olen's tribute, and the old quiet holds. The keepers breathe more easily, though not very easily.

focuses.name: The Warden League
focuses.desc: Mirolon's wardens have raised a league of the free south, and Olen is invited to join. The keepers bless the banner, and Olena rides to the league's first meeting with a lamp in her hand.

focuses.name: The Cliffs Hold
focuses.desc: The cliff forts are completed: stone towers at every landing, with winches, signal-fires and stocks of arrows. Olen can now be taken only by a fleet that is willing to lose half of itself.

focuses.name: The Breeze Healers
focuses.desc: Healers of the Breeze walk the cliff roads with lamps and herb-bags, tending the sick of every folk. They are honoured by the keepers and welcomed by everyone else.

focuses.name: Healers to Mirolon
focuses.desc: A company of healers travels north to the lake towns of Mirolon, bringing herbs, lamps and a calm that the wardens badly need. They are received with gratitude and a long list of patients.

focuses.name: Healers to the North
focuses.desc: Another company of healers is sent to the court of Aenor, where Olen's herbs are valued and its methods are studied. It is a small gift, and the court remembers it.

focuses.name: The Breeze Carries Word
focuses.desc: A pilgrim from the north reaches the cliffs with word of [zin_loc_eindil], whose road passes through the lands where the healers have worked. The keepers listen to the tale and add a verse to the evening song.

focuses.name: The Breeze Guard
focuses.desc: The guard of the cliff shrines is raised from the sons of the keepers, armed with spears and shown how to hold a path. They wear white cloaks and march in step.

focuses.name: Cliff Archers
focuses.desc: Archers are posted along the cliff-tops with long bows and quivers of fletched cane. A boat that tries to land below them is shot to pieces before the keel touches shingle.

focuses.name: The Sea Watch
focuses.desc: Lamps burn on the cliff-tops through the night, and watchers sit beside each. A hull on the horizon is seen long before it can be named.

focuses.name: Guard of the Breeze
focuses.desc: The guard is drawn together into a single body under Captain Joss Ardel, with white cloaks and iron-rimmed shields. They are few, but they are steady.

focuses.name: The Breeze Turns
focuses.desc: The evening wind blows from the wrong quarter, and the keepers know what it means. War is coming to the cliffs, and Olena calls the people to the shrines.

focuses.name: Hold the Cliffs
focuses.desc: Every landing is manned, every path watched and every shrine garrisoned. The Breeze blows on, and Olen holds the cliffs it blows over.

focuses.name: The Shrines Shelter
focuses.desc: Refugees from the north climb to the shrines, footsore and hungry, with children on their backs. The keepers open the doors, and the cisterns, and the granaries.

focuses.name: The Breeze Returns
focuses.desc: The war moves on, and the evening wind blows from the sea once more. The keepers relight the lamps one by one, and the cliff-tops glow.
